name: Hu Moment Invariants
description: Computes Hu's seven moment invariants to detect shape and rotation anomalies in AI content (Hu, 1962).
mechanism:
This method computes Hu's (1962) moment invariants and extended affine moment invariants for forgery detection:

1. **Geometric Moment Computation**: Raw geometric moments mₚᵧ = ΣΣ xᵖyᵧI(x,y) are computed over image blocks. Central moments μₚᵧ are derived by shifting to the centroid, providing translation invariance.

2. **Hu Moment Invariant Extraction**: The seven Hu invariants (φ₁ through φ₇) are calculated from normalized central moments. These are invariant to translation, rotation, and scaling — properties that enable detection of copy-move forgery where copied regions may be geometrically transformed.

3. **Block-wise Invariant Mapping**: The image is divided into overlapping blocks and moment invariants are computed per block. Blocks with similar invariant vectors but different spatial locations suggest copy-move manipulation.

4. **Affine Moment Invariants (AMI)**: Extended invariants following Flusser et al. (2009) capture affine-invariant features, detecting copies that have undergone shearing or non-uniform scaling beyond simple rotation.

5. **Consistency Analysis**: Moment invariant distributions across the image are analyzed for statistical anomalies. Natural images show smooth spatial variation in moment features, while AI-generated images may exhibit unnatural uniformity or discontinuities at generation boundaries. The final score quantifies deviation from expected natural moment statistics.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models

references.title: Hu, M.K. (1962). Visual Pattern Recognition by Moment Invariants. IRE Trans. Information Theory.
Flusser, J. et al. (2009). Moments and Moment Invariants in Pattern Recognition. Wiley.
